label: Similarity assumptions imply distinct limb-bone area and circumference exponents
notation: geometric: A \propto M^{2/3}, C \propto M^{1/3}; elastic: A \propto M^{3/4}, C \propto M^{3/8}; stress: A \propto M, C \propto M^{1/2}
assumptions: Positive body mass; circular cross-sections; each similarity model's diameter power law; for posture, force proportional to mass, effective mechanical advantage e M^γ, and constant nonzero stress.
scope_note: Proves the target exponents and the posture correction A ∝ M^(1−γ), conditional on explicit similarity assumptions. It does not establish which model animals follow or Thompson's empirical upper-size claim; those require data.

label: Femoral wall thickness follows bending moment along the shaft
notation: wall thickness t(x) \propto bending moment M(x), maximal at mid-shaft
reason: The approach formalizes cross-sectional allometry across body masses, not the claim's within-bone wall-thickness distribution or its bending-moment model.
